small_guidance:
- Sweep larger BLOCK_W (32, 64) combined with tiling along the output-channel axis (BLOCK_OC=8/16) so the (OC×BLOCK_W) accumulator tile stays in registers; current code always allocates (16×BLOCK_W) which limits occupancy — try processing two (dp,hp) pairs per program to amortize weight loads.
- Add autotune configs with num_warps=4/8 and num_stages=3/4 keyed on (N,Dp,Hp,Wp); also try grouping the 8 (ddp,dhp,dwp) sub-positions so the inner IC×KD×KH×KW weight loads are reused across all 8 outputs (load weight tile once, broadcast to 8 accumulators).
- Pre-pack weights into shape (OC, IC, KD, KH, KW) contiguous along OC so `tl.load(w_ptr + offs_oc*...)` becomes a single contiguous vector load instead of strided; current layout has OC stride = KD*KH*KW which is non-coalesced.
large_guidance:
- Switch from "gather conv-transpose" (current) to a scatter-add formulation in a separate kernel that writes the full conv-transpose output, then fuse maxpool+softmax+sub+swish+chan-max in a second kernel. With stride=2, only 1 or 2 of the 3 kernel taps contribute per output position; an explicit scatter from input×weight outer product hits every multiply exactly once and avoids the parity-masked loads currently wasting work.
- Alternatively, reformulate as an implicit-GEMM: tile output as (N·Dp·Hp·Wp_tile, OC) with K=IC·KD·KH·KW, use `tl.dot` for the OC×BLOCK_W accumulate instead of the manual broadcast outer product. The current `wv[:,None]*xv[None,:]` doesn't use tensor cores; an FP16/TF32 dot through `tl.dot` would cut compute time substantially on the 4090.
- Fuse the 8 spatial sub-positions of one maxpool window into a single program that keeps the OC×8 accumulators resident, runs the softmax/sub/swish/chan-max once per maxpool output, and stores one fp32 — reducing the chan-reduction overhead which currently runs 8× per output (one per ddp,dhp,dwp inside the maxpool tree).
